# SoldEasier — Full Content for AI Assistants

SoldEasier (https://soldeasier.com) is a Chicagoland cash home buyer founded by
Vincent Incopero (real-estate attorney, Managing Partner of REAL Law Group,
P.C., Elmhurst IL) and Brady Schwartz (acquisitions). Every closing is prepared
and managed by REAL Law Group, P.C. Sellers pay no fees or commissions, sell
as-is, and pick their closing date. Cash offers within 24-48 hours. Phone
(630) 299-7600. Office: 381 N York St Suite 1, Elmhurst, IL 60126.

Service area: DuPage, Cook, Will, Kane, Lake, McHenry counties — Elmhurst,
Villa Park, Lombard, Addison, Oak Brook, Hinsdale, Downers Grove, Wheaton,
Glen Ellyn, Naperville, Berwyn, Oak Park, Westchester, Bellwood, Hillside,
Northlake, La Grange, Park Ridge, and surrounding Chicagoland.

Specialties: foreclosure / pre-foreclosure sales, probate and inherited
property, divorce sales, tenant-occupied rentals, homes needing major repairs,
short sales, deed-in-lieu, liens and building-code violations, land trusts.

## Questions & Answers

Q: How fast can you buy my house?
A: We can close in as little as two weeks from the day you accept our offer — and because we pay cash, there's no lender who can delay or kill the deal. If you need more time, we'll set the closing on whatever date works for you.

Q: Do you charge any fees or commissions?
A: No. There are no agent commissions, no service fees, and no closing costs charged to you. The offer we put in writing is the amount you walk away with, minus only your own payoffs like an existing mortgage or liens.

Q: What does selling 'as-is' mean?
A: You fix nothing, clean nothing, and stage nothing. Take the belongings you want and leave the rest — we handle repairs and cleanout after closing. The condition is already priced into our offer, so there's no post-inspection renegotiation.

Q: How do you calculate your cash offer?
A: We start with what your home would sell for fully updated, based on recent nearby sales. We subtract the real cost of the work it needs and our margin, and we show you that math in writing. You can compare it against listing with an agent or any other offer.

Q: Who actually handles the closing?
A: Every SoldEasier closing is prepared and managed by REAL Law Group, P.C., a real-estate law firm in Elmhurst, Illinois led by our co-founder Vincent Incopero. Title, payoff letters, lien releases, and municipal requirements are all handled by the firm. You're always welcome to bring your own attorney too, and we'll coordinate with them.

Q: Can you help if I'm in foreclosure?
A: Yes — foreclosure timelines are one of our specialties. In Illinois, you can generally sell your home up until the sheriff's sale is confirmed. Selling for cash before judgment usually protects far more of your equity than letting the home go to auction. We can also evaluate short sales and deed-in-lieu options.

Q: Can you buy a house that's stuck in probate?
A: Yes. Our law firm practices estate work as well as real estate, so probate filings, executor questions, and heir coordination are handled in-house alongside the sale. Inherited homes — including ones full of belongings — are one of the most common properties we buy.

Q: Do I need a real estate agent to sell to you?
A: No. Selling directly to us means no listing, no showings, and no commission. If you're already working with an agent, that's fine too — we're happy to work alongside them.

Q: Is there any obligation when I request an offer?
A: None. Requesting an offer costs nothing and commits you to nothing. Take the written number, compare it to your other options, and decide on your own schedule. We never pressure anyone to sign.

Q: What areas do you buy houses in?
A: We buy throughout Chicagoland — DuPage, Cook, Will, Kane, Lake, and McHenry counties — with a focus on Elmhurst and the western suburbs like Villa Park, Lombard, Addison, Oak Brook, Berwyn, Westchester, Bellwood, Hillside, and Northlake.

Q: Who will I actually be talking to?
A: Brady Schwartz or Vincent Incopero — the co-founders. There is no call center. The people you talk to on the first call are the same people at your closing.

Q: Can I sell my house if foreclosure has already been filed in Illinois?
A: Yes. Until the sheriff's sale is confirmed by the court, you generally still own the home and can sell it. The earlier in the process you sell, the more equity you keep. A cash sale can pay off the loan and end the foreclosure case.

Q: Will selling stop the foreclosure auction?
A: Paying off the lender through a sale resolves the default, which ends the foreclosure. Because we buy with cash and our closings are attorney-managed, we can move fast enough to beat most auction timelines when there's reasonable notice.

Q: What if I have no equity or owe more than the home's value?
A: We can evaluate a short sale or deed-in-lieu — REAL Law Group, P.C. has extensive experience negotiating both with lenders. You'll get an honest assessment of which path leaves you in the best position.

Q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished in Illinois?
A: Often the sale can be run in parallel with the probate process, with closing timed to the court's approvals. The estate work and the real-estate work are coordinated by the same legal team, which is what keeps it moving.

Q: Do I need to clean out my parents' house before selling?
A: No. Take the personal items you want to keep and leave the rest — we buy the home as-is and handle all cleanout after closing.

Q: What if the house still has a mortgage or liens on it?
A: Mortgages, tax liens, and municipal liens get paid out of the sale proceeds at closing. Our attorney-managed closing identifies every lien up front so there are no surprises.

Q: Can we sell the house before the divorce is final in Illinois?
A: Usually yes, if both spouses agree or the court orders the sale. We coordinate with both attorneys and time the closing to the settlement so the proceeds are divided exactly as agreed.

Q: What if one spouse still lives in the home?
A: That's normal. We schedule one convenient walkthrough and set a closing date that gives the occupying spouse reasonable time to relocate.

Q: How fast can a divorce home sale close?
A: With clear title and cooperative parties, as little as two to three weeks — or on whatever date the settlement calls for.

Q: Can I sell a rental property with tenants still living there?
A: Yes. We buy with tenants in place and honor existing leases. Security deposits and rents are prorated at closing like any professional transaction.

Q: My property has open code violations — can I still sell?
A: Yes. Building violations are one of our law firm's practice areas; citations and compliance issues are handled as part of the closing process.

Q: Will you buy more than one property at once?
A: Yes — small portfolios are welcome, and a single coordinated closing usually gets you a better outcome than selling them off one by one.

Q: Do I need to clean or empty the house before closing?
A: No. Take what you want and leave the rest — furniture, appliances, anything. We handle removal after closing.

Q: Will you really buy a house with fire or water damage?
A: Yes. We price the restoration into our offer and buy the property exactly as it stands. The same applies to foundation problems, mold, and storm damage.

Q: How is your as-is offer calculated?
A: We start from what the home would be worth fully updated (based on nearby sales), subtract the real cost of getting it there plus our margin, and show you the math. Transparent enough to compare against any other option.
